name: Lavender Blush
lede: Lavender Blush is an almost-white pink, one of the 140 named colors of the X11 set that web browsers adopted as CSS keywords.

sections.title: A web keyword
sections.body: Paterson lists LavenderBlush as one of the colours in the X11 Color Set, with the hex code FFF0F5 [1]. The set is a screen standard, so the name describes a tint on a display, not a dye or a pigment [1]. Like all hex values for named colors it is an approximation and will shift between displays [1].

sections.title: Next to white
sections.body: Our library gives it the sources CSS and Wikipedia only, and its nearest everyday name is white, about eight and a half units away [2]. Close neighbors in the same corner are [[misty-rose]], [[linen]] and [[lavender]], which shares its first word [2].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: The pale tint turns up in 26 of 23,781 museum paintings, about 0.11 per cent [3]. Within a painting it most often plays a light, in 87 per cent of the 15 paintings measured by lightness rank [3]. It peaks in the 1800s, but at 0.8 times the expected rate for the same museums, so no era favors it [3]. The earliest dated painting is from 1423, by Gentile da Fabriano [3].
